parsed.summary: PLAN-B75 successfully addresses all previous round findings (R1 & R2) and satisfies all user requirements without introducing look-ahead bias or statistical errors. The transition from wave invalidation to key turning points (K1-K3) is pre-registered with strict FDR control (BH q < 0.10) and practical distance constraints. The TX continuous contract and night-session pipeline correctly binds night sessions (15:00 T-1 to 05:00 T) to trading date T, eliminating settlement-day splits. Post-close chip factors properly account for overnight returns and use tradable next-day open prices. Low-resource 512MB streaming limits, UTC epoch timestamps with Asia/Taipei LWC formatters, and fallback mechanisms are sound.

findings.issue: For TAIEX cash index (TWII) 5-minute bars, TAIFEX zip only covers futures (TX). If Cnyes fails to fetch TWII intraday 5m bars, the plan relies on startup backfill from Yahoo (^TWII 5m 60d), but does not explicitly schedule a Yahoo fallback if Cnyes fails at 13:50.
findings.suggestion: In the 13:50 or 16:30 schedule, if TWII bars5 for the current day are incomplete (< 54 bars) and Cnyes retry fails, allow a fallback fetch to Yahoo Finance (^TWII 5m) to ensure cash index intraday data remains uninterrupted.

findings.issue: On Taiwan national holidays where Friday night has a session running until Saturday 05:00 but the following Monday is a holiday, the next trading day T is Tuesday rather than Monday.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the trading day resolver maps the Saturday 05:00 night session to the actual next open trading day as verified by FinMind's fut_daily calendar, rather than assuming Monday.

parsed.coverage: Verified sections 1-13 with special focus on key level selection criteria (§2), futures continuous roll and ref_close (§3.2), low-memory streaming (§3.5), intraday timeframes & timezone handling (§4.1), session state detection (§5), post-close chip factor testing methodology (§6.1), composite direction aggregation (§6.2), and test suites (§11).
parsed.limitations: Review is based on code context in service.py, levels.py, engine.py and PLAN-B75 specifications. Execution performance of TAIFEX zip parsing on Fly.io 512MB RAM will depend on network throughput and CPU throttling during concurrent web traffic.
